Traditional support lookup tasks and structured BI-style questions differ in data source, query form, processing, and output in this corpus.

- **Traditional support lookup tasks** are direct natural-language queries against policy, SOP, and troubleshooting documentation. Examples include policy lookup, onboarding procedure checks, troubleshooting assistance, and course verification [NL-028#NL-028-S06]. TutorChat processes these through semantic query processing, vector search over KnowledgeHub, permission filtering, reranking, and grounded synthesis with inline citations [NL-002#NL-002-S03]. These are classed as “direct lookup” queries in the validation Golden Dataset, making up 40% of the test set [NL-008#NL-008-S08]. If no supporting evidence exists, the system must return an insufficient-evidence response rather than guess [NL-008#NL-008-S04].

- **Structured BI-style questions** are SQL aggregation queries over tabular telemetry, such as `support_tickets` and `customer_satisfaction_log`. Examples include summing ticket counts by category, averaging ticket counts by segment, extracting high-priority tickets open over 48 hours, and calculating average CSAT by plan tier [NL-029#NL-029-S07]. These return computed, tabular metrics for operational reporting and are designed to be run programmatically by analysts, rather than answered as document-grounded conversational prose [NL-029#NL-029-S07].
